key_insight: A recursive deep learning pipeline can replace slow finite-element simulation to predict the transverse compression response and modulus of synthetic plant fibers from their cross-sections.
engineering_relevance: This enables high-throughput screening of natural-fiber reinforcements, helping engineers design more reliable bio-based composites despite large microstructural variability.
method: Generate 1,000 synthetic hemp-like fiber geometries, including cases with and without a lumen.
Use two coupled recursive U-Nets to predict the stepwise evolution of deformation and internal stress under transverse compression.
Feed the final stress field into a regression CNN to estimate transverse Young's modulus.
evidence_signal: Against FE ground truth, the model achieved SSIM 0.9574 ± 0.0074 and RMSE 0.0345 ± 0.0079 for stress-field evolution, and predicted modulus with R² = 0.938 ± 0.024, MAE = 24.31 ± 1.23 MPa, and MAPE = 5.25 ± 0.91%, while inference took under one second per fiber versus about five minutes for FE.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on synthetically generated fibers trained against FE data, so real-world transfer to experimental microstructures and out-of-distribution geometries still needs validation.
paper_title: Deep Learning-based Mechanical Characterization of Synthetically Generated Plant Fibers under Transverse Compression
